name: Floss and interdental cleaners (floss, picks, interdental brushes, woodsticks)
anchor: sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant schedules with the Germany BVL 2017 TOOTHPASTE tier as the oral-mucosal anchor for formulated products, and Canada SOR/2018-83's mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling as the article anchor
native_basis: oral-care article as placed on market (total content per accessible part, ug/kg)
native_basis_label: oral-care article as placed on market — total heavy-metal content of each accessible part, per unit mass of that component's material (ug/kg). Not a cosmetic finished-product basis, not a dietary maximum level, and not an EN 71-3 migration/leachate value.
scope_note: Dental floss and tape, floss picks and harps, interdental brushes, woodsticks and rubber interdental picks, and floss threaders. These are ARTICLES and no cosmetic finished-product contaminant limit reaches them, notwithstanding that many carry a wax, flavour or fluoride coating; the coating is sampled as its own component rather than treated as a cosmetic in its own right. The applicable instrument is the article-scoped mouth-contact lead ceiling; every other analyte is held under component-level control. Interdental brush wire is the highest-risk component in the row because it is a nickel-bearing stainless steel in direct, abrasive mucosal contact.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(cosmetic|migration|leachate|colourant|colorant|surface coating|sticker|as consumed|wet weight|candy))(?=.*(content in accessible part|concentration by weight in article))
basis_guard_note: An oral-care article is not a cosmetic and is not a food. The guard admits only article material-content instruments (Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible-part lead content; REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) lead concentration by weight in a mouthable article) and rejects (a) finished-cosmetic impurity limits, which are written for a formulated product and cannot be applied to a polymer filament or a stainless-steel staple, (b) EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy values, which are MIGRATION limits and would understate content by orders of magnitude if read as content, and (c) surface-coating and sticker instruments, which govern an applied film rather than the substrate.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), Category 20 Oral Care: a formulated oral product takes the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant maximum in its as-sold basis, with the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier read across to non-toothpaste oral-mucosal forms where it is stricter; an oral-care article takes the Canadian mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling and is otherwise held under component-level control. Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: total lead content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material (article content basis, not migration)
Pb.label: Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83) reach mouth-contact consumer products, and section 2(1) caps EACH ACCESSIBLE PART of such a product at 90 mg/kg total lead. An oral-care article is a consumer product brought into contact with the user's mouth in the course of normal use, so the Canadian value directly regulates this cell on the article's own content basis. The only other article-scoped sovereign lead CONTENT instrument in the register, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628, sets 0.05% lead by weight (500 mg/kg) for articles that may be placed in the mouth by children; it is five and a half times looser and does not bind.
Pb.substantiation: The Canadian ceiling is applied to every accessible part of the finished article, not to a composite of the whole product, because that is how section 2(1) is written; a composite-averaged result would dilute a leaded component against inert bulk and is not accepted. Components tested separately: the filament or yarn (PTFE, nylon or silk), the wax, flavour or fluoride coating on it, the interdental brush wire and its polymer coating, the pick or handle polymer, any wooden or bamboo stick, and any accessible metal cutter on the dispenser. The coating is sampled separately from the filament because flavour, wax and fluoride coatings carry their own mineral and pigment inputs and would be diluted below detection in a whole-product composite. Two allowances written into the cited instruments are deliberately NOT taken: SOR/2018-83 section 2(2)'s conditional essential-characteristic exception, which substitutes a release criterion for the content criterion, and the REACH entry 63(8)(g) brass-alloy derogation at 0.5% lead by weight. Both are machinability and functional-necessity allowances rather than health findings, and HMTc certifies against the content criterion without them. The EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are likewise not used: they are migration limits on a leachate basis, and reading a migration number as a content ceiling is the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent.

Cd.rationale: No sovereign sets a cadmium content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument that reaches this product form on a total-content basis, is lead-only; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: cadmium is a known pigment and polymer-stabiliser residue in coloured plastics and a plating-bath contaminant, both of which are present in this article class.
Cd.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-content analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, with COMPONENT-LEVEL sampling of the finished article (the filament or yarn (PTFE, nylon or silk), the wax, flavour or fluoride coating on it, the interdental brush wire and its polymer coating, the pick or handle polymer, any wooden or bamboo stick, and any accessible metal cutter on the dispenser) — each component digested and reported separately, with no composite-averaged result accepted. No numeric ceiling is published; results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context plus supplier corrective action on the identified component).

iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic and no jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for a consumer article; every sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum level is scoped to rice, fish or fruit juice. The cell is governed by reflex speciation off the total-arsenic control rather than by an invented ceiling.
iAs.reference_method: Reflex HPLC-ICP-MS inorganic-arsenic speciation on any component (the filament or yarn (PTFE, nylon or silk), the wax, flavour or fluoride coating on it, the interdental brush wire and its polymer coating, the pick or handle polymer, any wooden or bamboo stick, and any accessible metal cutter on the dispenser) whose total-arsenic screen is confirmed above the analytical reporting limit. The inorganic fraction is held under ALARA and triggers supplier corrective action on the identified component.

The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: mercury is a recognised trace in mineral pigments and in some plating and catalyst residues, so the cell is screened rather than assumed absent.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a polymer filament, elastomer, wood stick or stainless-steel component, and no jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for a consumer article. It is held as a control rather than registered as a speciation-bounded not-material determination because this row's total-mercury parent is itself a control with no published ceiling: a speciation-bounded claim requires a published total-element parent to bound the species against, and this row has none. Mercury is therefore governed through the total-mercury control.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold on each component (the filament or yarn (PTFE, nylon or silk), the wax, flavour or fluoride coating on it, the interdental brush wire and its polymer coating, the pick or handle polymer, any wooden or bamboo stick, and any accessible metal cutter on the dispenser). Methylmercury speciation (GC-ICP-MS, EPA 1630) is required only where a confirmed total-mercury result cannot be traced to an inorganic input.

The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: nickel is unambiguously material for this article class — stainless-steel filament staples, wires, tips and plated parts are nickel-bearing by construction and nickel is a contact sensitiser released on mucosal contact.

Cr.rationale: No sovereign sets a total chromium content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument that reaches this product form on a total-content basis, is lead-only; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: chromium is a defining alloying element of the stainless steel used for staples, wires and tips and is present in chrome plating and in Cr(III) pigments; total chromium is a screen for the Cr(VI) reflex below and is not itself protective.
Cr.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-content analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, with COMPONENT-LEVEL sampling of the finished article (the filament or yarn (PTFE, nylon or silk), the wax, flavour or fluoride coating on it, the interdental brush wire and its polymer coating, the pick or handle polymer, any wooden or bamboo stick, and any accessible metal cutter on the dispenser) — each component digested and reported separately, with no composite-averaged result accepted. Cr-VI.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium CONTENT limit for a consumer article; the EU toy figure (Directive 2009/48 Category II, 5 ug/kg) is a migration value on a leachate basis and cannot be read as a content ceiling without conflating the two, which this row's basis guard forbids. Cr(VI) is not registered as a method artifact here: chrome-plated and chromate-passivated metal parts, stainless-steel filament staples and orthodontic-grade wire are real Cr(VI) sources in mouth-contact articles, so an absence claim would not survive the substantiation gate. The cell is a control with reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex Cr(VI) speciation (EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with IC-ICP-MS per EPA 6800, or EN 15192) on any component (the filament or yarn (PTFE, nylon or silk), the wax, flavour or fluoride coating on it, the interdental brush wire and its polymer coating, the pick or handle polymer, any wooden or bamboo stick, and any accessible metal cutter on the dispenser) returning an elevated total-chromium screen. Any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails the lot and blocks release pending supplier corrective action.
